scriptures.title: Tantrāloka, Ch. 1
scriptures.subtitle: Abhinavagupta · Viveka of Jayaratha · tr. Dyczkowski (ch. 1)

passages.section: The Types of Liberating Knowledge (vijñānabhid)
passages.en:
May that (divine) abode - the Trika reality which is nonduality (itself)
and the full (and perfect) realisation of freedom - from which (proceed the
powers of) will, knowledge and action that are the immanent (udita) planes of
(transcendental) consciousness and bliss, and of which all this (universe), which
is such, is the (unfolding) glory of its unrestrained power, be (ever) present
within my mind, and (thereby) destroy (all that within it) obscures the secret of
the transmission (ägamarahasya) of Siva's teachings.2 (1)
passages.primaryEn: Abhinavagupta opens his great book with a prayer to the highest reality. In simple words: may that supreme home — the Trika truth which is pure oneness, and the complete experience of total freedom — always live in my heart. From this supreme reality come the three powers we all know: the power to wish (will), the power to know (knowledge) and the power to do (action). The whole universe is nothing but the shining play of its free power. And may this presence in my heart destroy everything that hides the secret wisdom of Lord Śiva's teachings. This one verse contains the entire book in seed form: oneness, freedom, the three powers, and the prayer to remove ignorance.

passages.section: The Types of Liberating Knowledge (vijñānabhid)
passages.en:
Liberated (as I am even whilst living) in the body, by the drops of compassion from the ocean of the venerable Kalyāņa (who is auspicious good
fortune), I take refuge in him, a true master, within (my) heart.4 (2)
passages.primaryEn: Here the author bows to his own master with deep love. In simple words: I am already free even while living in this body. How? By a few drops of compassion flowing like an ocean from my noble teacher Kalyāṇa, whose very name means good fortune. I take shelter in him, the true master, inside my heart. The commentary adds two precious points. First, the word 'means' (upāya) here does not mean outer rituals — it means the saving knowledge itself, the wisdom that carries you to freedom. Second, old books show this verse slightly differently, and the name Kalyāṇa is itself a blessing: the teacher is described as an ocean of good luck, and tradition remembers him as the master who taught Jayaratha, the commentator, merely by his loving glance.

passages.section: The Types of Liberating Knowledge (vijñānabhid)
passages.en:
Although (my) heart is hard with the burden of phenomenal existence, I
quickly place (there) His teaching that is borne on the head of all the kings of
the earth like a crown jewel. (3)
passages.primaryEn: The author speaks humbly about himself. In simple words: my heart has become hard and rough because of carrying the heavy load of worldly life for so long. Even so, I quickly place the Lord's teaching inside it — that teaching which sits like a shining crown jewel on the heads of all the kings of the earth. Meaning: this wisdom is the highest ornament; even kings bow to it. Though I feel unworthy and hard-hearted, I waste no time in sheltering this teaching within me.

passages.section: The Types of Liberating Knowledge (vijñānabhid)
passages.en:
I am not engaged (in this work) to attain (some) unique status as a
writer; nor (am I doing this) to show off (my) skill with language; rather my
desire is that (my) thought be purified (vikalpah samskāravān) by being
(constantly) occupied with this teaching (artha). (4)
passages.primaryEn: Abhinavagupta tells us honestly why he is writing this huge book — and it is not for fame. In simple words: I am not writing to become famous as an author, nor to show off my beautiful language. My only wish is that my own thinking becomes pure and clean by staying busy day and night with this holy teaching. The commentary explains the key phrase 'purified thought': cleaning the mind of restless doubts and fixing it on the truth is itself a spiritual practice, belonging to the path called the Empowered Means. So writing this book is the author's own meditation.

passages.section: The Types of Liberating Knowledge (vijñānabhid)
passages.en:
Some ignorant people are constantly coming and going (from this
world, life to life), others are envious, some in doubt - what should we say of
those who (can) hear that (teaching but) have not come (to listen)? (5)
passages.primaryEn: The author looks around at people with sadness and wonder. In simple words: some ignorant souls keep coming and going — taking birth again and again without learning. Others burn with jealousy. Some are full of doubt. But what can we even say about those people who get the rare chance to hear this liberating teaching, yet do not even come to listen? The message is gentle but sharp: this wisdom is precious and rare; ignoring it when it comes to your door is the greatest loss.

passages.section: The Types of Liberating Knowledge (vijñānabhid)
passages.en:
Not having heard that profound and pleasant teaching (artha), whatever
is said by others with an intense (desire to) incite (people) to act (as they wish
them to do, but) which derives its skill (only from their) own way of thinking
(and intentions) (svāśaya), (simply) makes the mind unstable. (6)
passages.primaryEn: Here is a warning about false teachers. In simple words: if a person has never truly heard this deep and sweet teaching, then whatever clever talk he gives to push people around — however skillful it sounds — comes only from his own selfish thinking and hidden motives, and it will only make listeners' minds shaky and confused. True teaching steadies the mind; clever talk destabilises it. So the seeker must check: does this teaching come from real wisdom, or only from someone's personal agenda?

passages.section: The Types of Liberating Knowledge (vijñānabhid)
passages.en:
Although my speech is powerless here (in this task), whatever
restriction may arise (on one's understanding of the teachings is not my fault,
rather) that is (all) the venerable expansion of the Supreme Lord's great bliss
(which both hides and reveals the truth). (7)
passages.primaryEn: The author closes his introduction with total humility. In simple words: my words are too weak for this great task. If you find anything hard to understand in this book, do not blame me for it — that difficulty is only the play of the Supreme Lord's own great bliss, which hides the truth and also reveals it, as He likes. The commentary adds the beautiful back-story: the teacher Kalyāṇa gave this wisdom to his student in one instant, simply through his loving glance — knowledge passed heart to heart, not through long speeches. And the word Trika itself is often lovingly called 'Half of Six', a secret name for this tradition. So the whole teaching is grace: hidden by the Lord, opened by the Lord, through the master's glance.

passages.section: The Initial Invocation
passages.mula:
विमलकलाश्रयाभिनवसृष्टिमहा जननी
भरिततनुश्च पञ्चमुखगुप्तरुचिर्जनकः
तदुभययामलस्फुरितभावविसर्गमयं
हृदयमनुत्तरामृतकुलं मम संस्फुरतात् ।। १ ।।
passages.en:
(My) mother, Vimalā, is (joyous with) the glory (of the festival of
my birth), the ever new (abhinava) creation, her foundation the pure
(vimala) energy (of the Moon). (My) father (Narasimhagupta) is the hidden
(protected) (gupta) light (ruci) with five faces and his body is full.7 May the
body (kula) of the nectar (amrta) of the Absolute (anuttara), my Heart, the
emission (visarga)," which is the vibrant (emissive) state of the united form
(yāmala) of both of them (my father and mother, Śiva and Śakti), pulsate
radiantly! (1)
passages.primaryEn: This is the famous first verse of the Tantrāloka, and it has two meanings at once — that is its beauty. In simple words: My mother Vimalā (whose name means Pure) found her greatest joy in giving birth to me; she lived in pure God-consciousness, and her energy is ever-fresh, always new. My father Narasimhagupta (his nickname means the hidden light with five faces) was a full, complete man with no empty desires, steady like the five-faced Lord. May my Heart — the divine juice (nectar) of the highest reality, born from the loving union of these two, Śiva and Śakti, father and mother — throb and shine everywhere! The commentaries open up every word: 'full-bodied' means containing everything like Lord Bhairava Himself; 'emission' (visarga) means consciousness endlessly pouring itself out and yet resting in itself — pure potential becoming everything; 'Heart' means the pulsing I-feeling where Śiva and Śakti are one; 'five faces' are the five powers — consciousness, bliss, will, knowledge and action — flowing into the world; 'ever-new' and 'hidden' are even hidden in the author's own name, Abhinava-gupta (ever-new + protected). Great masters read this verse in three ways at once: as praise of the supreme Goddess, as the union of Śiva and Śakti, and as the author's real human parents — all three true together.

passages.section: In Praise of the Deities
passages.mula:
नौमि चित्प्रतिभां देवीं परां भैरवयोगिनीम् ।
मातृमानप्रमेयांशशूलाम्बुजकृतास्पदाम् ।। २॥
passages.en:
I bow to the goddess Parā (the Supreme One), who is the creative
intuition of consciousness (citpratibhā).95 Bhairava's Yoginī (united with
Him) (bhairavayoginī), She has made (her) place on (top of) the lotuses (of
the Trika Trident, the) prongsgs96 of which are the aspects (of perception,
namely) subject, object and means of knowledge.7 (2)

passages.section: In Praise of the Deities
passages.mula:
नौमि देवीं शरीरस्थां नृत्यतो भैरवाकृतेः ।
प्रावृण्मेघघनव्योमविद्युल्लेखाविलासिनीम् ।। ३ ।।
passages.en: I bow to the goddess (Aparā), who resides in the body of Bhairava's dancing form107 and plays within it (like) a lightning flash in a sky (covered) with dense storm clouds.108 (3)

passages.section: In Praise of the Deities
passages.en: breasts. She has four arms and one face with three eyes. She is Supreme Śivā. (113-115)

passages.section: In Praise of the Deities
passages.mula:
दीप्तज्योतिश्छटाप्लुष्टभेदबन्धत्रयं स्फुरत् ।
स्ताज्ज्ञानशूलं सत्पक्षविपक्षोत्कर्तनक्षमम् ।। ४ ।।
passages.en:
'Located in the middle of the Triangle, she is placed within Vidyātattva. She is like the colour of dark blue lightning with the lustre of blue collyrium, divine (and beautiful), she has matted hair and is adorned with a tiara and jewels, she shines with (her) jewel earrings, she has three eyes and (wears) a brilliant blazing crown, and is beautiful with necklaces of conch shell and nacre around her neck. Rich with the beauty
of (her) pearl necklace and anklets, she possesses all the (auspicious) characteristics (of deity). She has eight arms and is adorned with many ornaments. On the right (there are in her hands) a (conch) shell (kambu), a sword, thread, and arrow. On the left a bow, a
shield, a skull, and a noose adorn (her). (21/200cd-204)
The weapons shine with the fire of time; licking up (and destroying with their flames), they are extremely hard to bear. She possesses many ornaments and is adorned
with many adornments. She is in her youth and is mad with passion, her breasts fat and
round. She is thin in the middle (at Her waist) and is endowed with (beautiful) hips. A
garland of skulls has been made (for her) that extends to (her) feet. She is mounted on
the Great Ghost (mahāpreta), and is made blissful with the bliss of nectar. She waves
her index finger, and is very fierce, characterized by all the (auspicious) characteristics.
Having worshipped Aparā,* who is in the middle of the Triangle, in this way,
linked to Vidyātattva and residing on the plane of the Foundation, and having worshipped the goddess, she fulfils all (one's) desires.' (Ibid. 21/204cd-209)
*All the manuscripts read 21/208c as evam parāparām dhyātvā ‘having
meditated in this way on Parāparā.' But this cannot be correct. Parāparā is red. Here this
goddess is clearly said to be 'black like a lightning cloud', which is the same analogy
Abhinava makes, drawing quite probably from some scriptural source. Thus, he glosses
the original description beautifully, saying that the darkness of the cloud is Bhairava's
body, whereas she is the lightning-like energy that flashes within it. Moreover, we are
told that this goddess resides on the lower plane of the foundation, which would be
appropriate for Aparã. Again, she is associated with Vidyātattva. This is the lowest of
the three tattvas comprising Vidyā, Ātma and Śiva. Clearly all these are indications that
confirm that the goddess described here is Aparā, not Parāparā.
May (Parāparā), the pulsingly radiant (sphurat) prong of knowledge, 4 that has burnt up the triple fetter with its blazing rays of the light (of Siva consciousness), have the power to uproot all that runs
contrary (vipakşa) to the truth (satpakşa),115 (4)

passages.section: In Praise of the Deities
passages.mula:
स्वातन्त्र्यशक्तिः क्रमसंसिसृक्षा
क्रमात्मता चेति विभोर्विभूतिः ।
तदेव देवीत्रयमन्तरास्ताम्
अनुत्तरं मे प्रथयत्स्वरूपम् ।। ५ ।
passages.en:
May that same triad of Goddesses - who are the glorious power of
the All-pervading Lord (vibhu) as 1) the power which is (His) freedom, 2)
the intent to emit the succession (krama) (of manifestation), and 3) the
succession (krama) itself123 - inwardly reveal my own (unsurpassable)
Anuttara124 nature (svabhāva). (5)

passages.section: In Praise of the Deities
passages.mula:
तद्देवताविभवभाविमहामरीचि-
चक्रेश्वरायितनिजस्थितिरेक एव ।
देवीसुतो गणपतिः स्फुरदिन्दुकान्तिः
सम्यक्समुच्छलयतान्मम संविदब्धिम् ।। ६ ।।
passages.en:
Moon. His own abiding state (nijasthiti) is to govern the Great Wheel of the
Rays (of the energies of Parā, Parāparā and Aparā)131 that exists by virtue
of the (unfolding and) glorious power (vibhava) of those deities. May he stir
(and lift) up the ocean of my consciousness thoroughly (to pervade the
universe and inspire me). (6)

passages.section: In Praise of the Teachers
passages.mula:
रागारुणं ग्रन्थिबिलावकीर्ण
यो जालमातानवितानवृत्ति ।
कलोम्भितं बाह्यपथे चकार
स्तान्मे स मच्छन्दविभुः प्रसन्नः ॥ ७ ॥
passages.en:
May the pervasive lord Macchanda (the Fisherman) be pleased
with me, he who cast along the outer path the net (of Māyā) that, red with
(colour and) attachment, fashioned (artistically) with (many) parts (kalā)
and strewn with knots and holes, spreads and extends (in all directions).143 (7)

passages.section: In Praise of the Teachers
passages.mula:
त्रैयम्बकाभिहितसन्ततिताम्रपर्णी-
सन्मौक्तिकप्रकरकान्तिविशेषभाजः
पूर्वे जयन्ति गुरवो गुरुशास्त्रसिन्धु-
कल्लोलकेलिकलनामलकर्णधाराः ।। ८
passages.en:
The ancient teachers triumph. Possessing the special beauty of the
multitude of authentic pearls from the Tāmraparņī (river)164 of the
That would not be correct, as Trika is Kaula. But it is true that the Tantric modality,
which is basic common Agamic Śaivism, is common to all, including Trika, that
encompasses both modalities.
Mountain in Karņataka to the end of Tamil Nadu in South India. Although the original
transmissions are said to take place on Mount Kailash, it is possible that Abhinava here
implicitly connects these teachers in some way with South India. Śambhunātha's
teacher, Sumati, is said to be from 'a sacred seat in the south' (dakşiņabhumipīțha) (see
below, 1/212cd-123ab and comm). We know from the Yasastilaka, which was written
by a Jain monk called Somadeva in South India in the ninth century, that Trika existed
there as a Kaula school that taught (no doubt amongst other things) basic Kaula practice,
i.e., sexual rites and the offerings of wine and meat to the Trika deities (see Dyczkowski
1988: 6). Maheśvarananada, who lived and wrote in South India around the 13th
century, quotes from a large number of Kashmir Śaiva texts as well as original Trika
and Krama sources known to Abhinavagupta, although not many Tantras. The Śrīvidyā
teachers like Amrtānanda and Śivānanda (who was Maheśvarananada's teacher) wrote
extensive commentaries on the Nityāşodaśikārņava (the Ocean of the Sixteen Nityā
(Yoginīs)) and the Yoginīhrdaya (the Heart of the Yoginīs), both root Tantras of the
Śrīvidyā (i.e., Tripurā) tradition, as well as independent works on the same subject.
They did this from the perspective of the Kashmiri masters, whom they knew very well
and quoted from extensively. The Krama system flourished there at least into the 14th
century. Important texts were written there. Amongst them are two called
Mahānayaprakāśa. One was written by Arņasimha, and the other by an unknown
author. Another great work was the Cidgaganacandrikā, by Śrīvatsa, who belonged to
Arņasimha's lineage. These were followed by Maheśvarānanda's Mahārthamañjarī, the
root verses of which are in early Maharastrian, revealed to Maheśvarānanda by a Yoginī
in the land of the Colas (modern Tamil Nadu) in the mystic state between waking and
dreaming (MM verse 71). The substantial number of works Maheśvarānanda quotes
unknown to the Kashmiris is testimony in itself to vigorous development there of these
traditions. However, in Kashmir itself, Muslim rule that was imposed from the middle
of the 14th century had largely brought a halt to further major developments. It seems
that some forms continued in the South practically up to the present day, mostly in
(spiritual) lineage named Traiyambaka, they are the stainless helmsmen (of
the boat that crosses) the ocean of the teachers' scripture, that heaves with
the play of (mighty) waves. (8)

passages.section: In Praise of the Teachers
passages.mula:
जयति गुरुरेक एव श्रीश्रीकण्ठो भुवि प्रथितः
तदपरमूर्तिर्भगवान् महेश्वरो भूतिराजश्च ।। ९ ।।
passages.en:
The venerable Śrīkaņțha, the one (unique) teacher who is well
known (prathita) in the world, triumphs, (as does) the lord (bhagavat)
Maheśvara,16 who is another of his forms, and Bhūtirāja170 (who is so also).
(9)

passages.section: In Praise of the Teachers
passages.mula:
श्रीसोमानन्दबोधश्रीमदुत्पलविनिःसृताः । जयन्ति संविदामोदसन्दभी दिक्प्रसर्पिणः ।। १० ॥
तदास्वादभरावेशबृंहितां मतिषट्पदीम् ।
गुरोर्लक्ष्मणगुप्तस्य नादसंमोहिनीं नुमः ।। ११ ।।
passages.en:
(The collections of fragrances (delighting) consciousness that come
forth from a beautiful blue lotus (utpala)187 by (its) blossoming with the joy of the (shining) moon which is beauty (itself), and spread in (all) directions,
excel (all). In the same way,) the compositions (inspired by) the bliss of consciousness, that have come forth from the venerable (śrīmat)188
Utpala(deva) by virtue of (his) awakening189 by the illustrious Somānanda,
and have spread in (all) directions, excel (all),190 (10)

passages.section: In Praise of the Teachers
passages.en:
We salute the bee-like mind of the teacher Lakşmanagupta, whose
sound is the attractive (resonance of consciousness) intensified by (his)
penetration (āveśa) into the copious relish of that (Lotus, his teacher
Utpaladeva).191 (11)

passages.section: In Praise of the Teachers
passages.mula:
यः पूर्णानन्दविश्रान्तः सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगः ।
स श्रीचुखुलको दिश्यादिष्टं मे गुरुरुत्तमः ।। १२ ।।
passages.en:
May the venerable Cukhulaka, the best of teachers who has crossed
over (and mastered) the purport of all the disciplines (sāstra) and rests in
perfect bliss, instruct me in what (I) desire (to learn).194 (12)

passages.section: In Praise of the Teachers
passages.mula:
जयताज्जगदुद्धृतिक्षमोऽसौ
भगवत्या सह शम्भुनाथ एकः ।
यदुदीरितशासनांशुभि
प्रकटोऽयं गहनोऽपि शास्त्रमार्गः ।। १३ ।।
passages.en:
jayatāj jagaduddhrtikşamo 'sau
May Śambhunātha who, together with Bhagavatī (his consort), is
the (only) one capable of extricating the (entire) universe (from ignorance),
be victorious! Although profound (and hard to grasp), it is he who has
made this path of the scriptures (śāstra) clear to me by the (enlightening)
rays of the teachings he has spoken (to me).197 (13)

passages.section: The Purpose of the Book and its Inspiration
passages.mula:
सन्ति पद्धतयश्चित्राः स्रोतोभेदेषु भूयसा ।
अनुत्तरषडधीर्थक्रमे त्वेकापि नेक्ष्यते ॥ १४ ॥
passages.en:
Many and various are the liturgical manuals (paddhati) (in use) in
the diverse currents (of scripture) (srotas),201 But there is not even one to be
seen for the procedures (krama) of the Anuttara Trika.202 (14)

passages.section: The Purpose of the Book and its Inspiration
passages.mula: इत्यहं बहुशः सद्भिः शिष्यसब्रहाचारिभिः । अर्थितो रचये स्पष्टां पूर्णार्थी प्रक्रियामिमाम् ।। १५ ॥
passages.en:
Thus, repeatedly requested by (those) virtuous people who are (my)
disciples and fellow students, I compose this treatise (prakriyā),203 which is
clear and complete (pūrņārthā).304 (15)

passages.section: The Purpose of the Book and its Inspiration
passages.mula:
श्रीभट्टनाथचरणाब्जयुगात्तथा श्री-
भट्टारिकांघ्रियुगलाद् गुरुसन्ततियी ।
बोधान्यपाशविषनुत्तदुपासनोत्थबोधोज्ज्वलोऽभिनवगुप्त इदं करोति ॥ १६ ॥
passages.en:
Abhinavagupta does this, flaming with the (awakened)
consciousness that has arisen by (devout) attendance (upāsana) to that
remedy for the poison of the fetters, namely (all) that is other than
(awakened) consciousness,205 which is (the teaching transmitted through
the) lineage of teachers (that has come) from the two lotus feet of the
venerable Bhațțanātha206 and the two feet of the venerable Bhațțārikā (his
consort). (16)

passages.section: The Purpose of the Book and its Inspiration
passages.mula:
न तदस्तीह यन्न श्रीमालिनीविजयोत्तरे ।
देवदेवेन निर्दिष्टं स्वशब्देनाथ लिङ्गतः ।। १७।।
passages.en:
There is nothing here (in the Tantrāloka) not taught by the God of gods in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara (Tantra), whether (directly) in His
own words or (indirectly) by allusion (lingatah).221 (17)

passages.section: The Purpose of the Book and its Inspiration
passages.mula:
दशा टादशवस्वष्टभिन्नं यच्छासनं विभोः ।
तत्सारं त्रिकशास्त्रं हि तत्सारं मालिनीमतम् ।। १८॥
passages.en:
The teaching (śāsana) of the pervasive Lord is divided into (groups of) ten, eighteen and eight times eight (Tantras), the essence of which is the
Trika scriptures (śāstra), and the essence of that is the Mālinīmata.224 (18)

passages.en: night in the dark lunar fortnight (when there is no moon) attains Bhairava's nature.' (87)

passages.section: The Purpose of the Book and its Inspiration
passages.mula: अदृष्टं प्रकटीकुर्मो गुरुनाथाज्ञया वयम् ।। १९ ।।
passages.en:
Thus, at the command of (our) master and protector (gurunātha),319
we will elucidate all that is contained herein 320 that has not been seen
(adrşta)321 by the learned who are devoid of the tradition
(sampradāyojjhita).322 (19)

passages.section: The Purpose of the Book and its Inspiration
passages.mula:
अभिनवगुप्तस्य कृतिः
सेयं यस्योदिता गुरुभिराख्या
त्रिनयनचरणसरोरुहचिन्तनलब्धप्रसिद्धिरिति ।। २० ।।
passages.en:
abhinavaguptasya krtih
This is the work of Abhinavagupta who, as declared by (his)
teachers, is a man who has attained the most excellent accomplishment
(and fame) (prasiddhi)325 by reflecting (and meditating) on (cintana) the
lotus326 feet of (his teacher, the) Three-Eyed One. (20)

passages.section: The Purpose of the Book and its Inspiration
passages.mula:
श्रीशम्भुनाथभास्करचरणनिपातप्रभापगतसङ्कोचम्
अभिनवगुप्तहृदम्बुज -
मेतद्विचिनुत महेशपूजनहेतोः ।। २१ ।।
passages.en:
abhinavaguptahrdambujam
In order to worship Maheśa (the Great Lord), discern (vicinuta)328
this, the lotus of Abhinavagupta's heart, that has blossomed 329 by the light falling from the feet330 of the sun-like Śambhunātha. (21)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
इह तावत्समस्तेषु शास्त्रेषु परिगीयते ।
अज्ञानं संसृते हेतुज्ञानं मोक्षैककारणम् ।। २२ ॥
passages.en:
Well then, it is proclaimed here (unanimously) in all the scriptures
that ignorance is the cause of transmigration, and knowledge is the sole
cause of liberation (from it). (22)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
मलमज्ञानमिच्छन्ति संसाराङ्करकारणम्
इति प्रोक्तं तथा च श्रीमालिनीविजयोत्तरे ।। २३।।
passages.en:
substance as the dualists maintain).347 It is the cause of (Karma, which is)
the sprout of transmigratory existence (samsāra), 348 (23)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
विशेषणेन बुद्धिस्थे संसारोत्तरकालिके ।
सम्भावनां निरस्यैतदभावे मोक्षमब्रवीत् ॥ २४।।
passages.en:
Once having precluded the possibility (that knowledge) present in
the intellect, which is subsequent to (the fettered state of) transmigration,
(is liberating,) by specifying (that ignorance is 'the cause of the sprout of
transmigration',) (the Lord) said that liberation (is achieved even) when
that (intellectual knowledge) is absent. (24)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
अज्ञानमिति न ज्ञानाभावश्चातिप्रसङ्गतः ।
स हि लोष्ठादिकेऽप्यस्ति न च तस्यास्ति संसृतिः ।। २५।।
passages.en:
(According to us,) ignorance is not a (total) lack of knowledge, for
(if that were so, the use of the term) would be too extensive. That
(ignorance) is also (present) in a stone and the like, and that is not subject
to transmigration. (25)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula: ज्ञानमेव तदज्ञानं शिवसूत्रेषु भासितम् ।। २६।।
passages.en: true nature of the object of knowledge (jñeya) in its totality (sāmastyena),367 (26)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
चैतन्यमात्मा ज्ञानं च बन्ध इत्यत्र सूत्रयोः ।
संश्लेषेतरयोगाभ्यामयमर्थः प्रदर्शितः ॥ २७॥
passages.en:
This is the point made by reading the aphorisms 'the Self is
consciousness' and 'knowledge is bondage' alternatively, together and separately.369 (27)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
चैतन्यमिति भावान्तः शब्दः स्वातन्त्र्यमात्रकम्
अनाक्षिप्तविशेषं सदाह सूत्रे पुरातने ।। २८ ।।
द्वितीयेन तु सूत्रेण क्रियां वा करणं च वा ।
ब्रुवता तस्य चिन्मात्ररूपस्य द्वैतमुच्यते ।। २९ ॥
द्वैतप्रथा तदज्ञानं तुच्छत्वाद्बन्ध उच्यते ।
तत एव समुच्छेद्यमित्यावृत्त्यानिरूपितम् ।। ३० ।।
passages.en: 'ignorance is bondage'). (28-30)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
स्वतन्त्रात्मातिरिक्तस्तु तुच्छोऽतुच्छोऽपि कश्चन ।
न मोक्षो नाम तन्नास्य पृथङनामापि गृह्यते ।। ३१ ।।

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
यत्तु ज्ञेयसतत्त्वस्य पूर्णापूर्णप्रथात्मकम् ।
तदुत्तरोत्तरं ज्ञानं तत्तत्संसारशान्तिदम् ।। ३२।।
passages.en:
The perception of the object of knowledge, along with the
metaphysical principles that constitute it, which is full or less complete,386 is
the knowledge that, increasingly higher, quells each corresponding (form
of) transmigratory existence,387 (32)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
रागाद्यकलुषोऽस्म्यन्तः शून्योऽहं कर्तृतोज्झितः ।
इत्थं समासव्यासाभ्यां ज्ञानं मुञ्चति तावतः ।। ३३ ।।
passages.en:
rāgādyakaluşo 'smy antahśūnyo 'ham kartrtojjhitah
"I am unsullied by attachment and the like", "I am inwardly
empty" and I am not an agent2392 - this kind of knowledge, whether
collectively or individually (samāsavyāsābhyām), liberates from (only) that
much (bondage).393 (33)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.en: proceeds from (their) union. (19-21)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.en:
In my opinion nobody is more modest than Nature. Knowing that "I have been
seen", she no more comes within the sight of the Self. Thus verily the Self is never
bound, nor is he released, nor does he transmigrate. It is Nature, being the support of
this manifold creation, that migrates, is bound and is released. (61-62)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.en:
The one Self thinks "I have seen her" and therefore loses all interest. The other
(i.e. Nature) thinks "I have been seen" and ceases to act further. Therefore, even if there
is still a connection, there is no reason for any further transformations.' (66)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.en: he goes to his own (corresponding) plane.' (11/73)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.en:
With the words 'his Self pure with the knowledge (that comes) from initiation',
a peculiarity is indicated with respect to the Mausula and Kāruka, who are dedicated
solely to the aforementioned Vow predominantly based on ritual. Their nature is,
respectively that of Tejeśa and Dhruva. As was said before: 'Tejeśa and Dhruva is the
supreme plane of the Pramāņas.' (10/1174)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
तस्मान्मुक्तोऽप्यवच्छेदादवच्छेदान्तरस्थितेः ।
अमुक्त एव मुक्तस्तु सर्वावच्छेदवर्जितः ॥ ३४॥
passages.en:
Therefore, even though (someone may be) free from (one) limitation
(avaccheda), he is not liberated because other limitations continue to exist.
He who is truly liberated is free of all limitations.425 (34)

passages.section: Concerning Freedom and Bondage, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
यत्तु ज्ञेयसतत्त्वस्य ज्ञानं सर्वात्मनोज्झितम् ।
अवच्छेदैर्न तत्कुत्राप्यज्ञानं सत्यमुक्तिदम् ।। ३५।।
passages.en: Knowledge of the object of knowledge (jñeya), along with the metaphysical principles that constitute it (satattva), free in all respects from limitations,434 (does not admit the persistence of) ignorance anywhere. (As such,) it bestows true liberation. (35)

passages.section: Concerning the Knower, Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
ज्ञानाज्ञानस्वरूपं यदुक्तं प्रत्येकमप्यदः ।
द्विधा पौरुषबौद्धत्वभिदोक्तं शिवशासने ।। ३६ ।।
passages.en:
(pauruşa) (which is constitutive of individual consciousness) and intellectual
(bauddha) (which is on the level of the conscious mind),435 (36)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
तत्र पुंसो यदज्ञानं मलाख्यं तज्जमप्यथ ।
स्वपूर्णचित्क्रियारूपशिवतावरणात्मकम् ।। ३७।।
सङ्कोचि क्क्रियारूपं तत्पशोरविकल्पितम् ।
तदज्ञानं न बुद्धयंशोऽध्यवसायाद्यभावतः ।। ३८ ।।
अहमित्थमिदं वेद्मीत्येवमध्यवसायिनी ।
षट्कचुकाबिलाणूत्थप्रतिबिम्बनतो यदा ।। ३९ ।। धीजीयते तदा तादृग्ज्ञानमज्ञानशब्दितम् ।
बौद्ध तस्य च तत्पस्नं पोषणीयं च पोष्ट च ।।
४० ।।
passages.en: spiritual and intellectual ignorance feed on one another). (39-40)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
क्षीणे तु पशुसंस्कारे पुंसः प्राप्तपरस्थितेः ।
विकस्वरं तद्विज्ञानं पौरुषं निर्विकल्पकम् ।। ४१ ।।
विकस्वराविकल्पात्मज्ञानौचित्येन यावसा ।
तबौद्धं यस्य तत्पस्नं प्राग्वत्पोष्यं च पोष्ट च ।। ४२ ॥
passages.en:
to
Spiritual knowledge is the expanding consciousness (vijñāna) devoid
of thought constructs of the individual soul who has attained (its original)
supreme state, as the latent trace (samskāra) of his (lower) fettered state
wanes away. The (liberating) insight (avasā) (that develops) in accord with
(the plenitude of) this expanding knowledge of the Self, free of thought
constructs, is intellectual knowledge (on the level of the conscious mind), of
which spiritual (knowledge) is, as before, (both) nourished (by it) and
nourishes (it). (Thus, spiritual and intellectual knowledge nourish one
another). (41-42)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
तत्र दीक्षादिना पाँस्नमज्ञानं ध्वंसि यद्यपि ।
तथापि तच्छरीरान्ते तज्ज्ञानं व्यज्यते स्फुटम् ।। ४३॥
passages.en:
465There (in that context) although spiritual ignorance (constitutive
of individual consciousness) is destroyed by initiation and the rest (that
follows), even so (without spiritual knowledge), that knowledge (of the Self)
manifests explicitly (only) when the body 466 comes to an end. (43)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
बौद्धज्ञानेन तु यदा बौद्धमज्ञानजृम्भितम् ।
विलीयते तदा जीवन्मुक्तिः करतले स्थिता ।। ४४।।
passages.en:
(However), liberation whilst still alive (in the body) is (as if) in the
palm of one's hand, if (all that has) developed out of intellectual ignorance
(on the level of the conscious mind) dissolves away by (sound) intellectual
knowledge (which is the self-realisation that results through insight into the
ultimate purport of the scriptures),481 (44)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
दीक्षापि बौद्धविज्ञानपूर्वी सत्यं विमोचिका ।
तेन तत्रापि बौद्धस्य ज्ञानस्यास्ति प्रधानता ।। ४५।।
passages.en:
Even initiation is truly (satyam)488 liberating (only if it is) preceded
by (clear) intellectual insight (bauddhavijñāna). Thus, there (in that case)
also, it is intellectual knowledge that is fundamental. (45)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
ज्ञानाज्ञानगतं चैतद्वित्वं स्वायम्भुवे रुरौ ।
मतङ्गादौ कृतं श्रीमत्खेटपालादिदैशिकैः ।। ४६ ।।
passages.en:
These two (aspects of) knowledge and ignorance have been
distinguished (from one another) by (Saiddhāntika) teachers, beginning
with the venerable Khețapāla, in (their commentaries) on the Ruru,493
Svāyambhuva, and Matanga amongst others.494 (46)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
तथाविधावसायात्मबौद्धविज्ञानसम्पदे ।
शास्त्रमेव प्रधानं यज्ज्ञेयतत्त्वप्रदर्शकम् ।। ४७ ।।
passages.en:
Scripture (śāstra), which reveals516 the (true) nature of (all) that
needs be known (jñeyatattva),517 is indeed the principal (factor) that serves
to bring about the intellectual understanding which is that kind of
(liberating) insight (avasāyā),518 (47)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
दीक्षया गलितेऽप्यन्तरज्ञाने पौरुषात्मनि
धीगतस्यानिवृत्तत्वाद्विकल्पोऽपि हि सम्भवेत् ।। ४८ ।।
passages.en:
Even when inner spiritual ignorance has (inwardly) ceased by
virtue of initiation, (binding) thought would (nevertheless still) arise
because (the ignorance) present in the intellect has not ceased. 520 (48)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
देहसद्भावपर्यन्तमात्मभावो यतो धियि ।
देहान्तेऽपि न मोक्षः स्यात्पौरुषाज्ञानहानितः ।। ४९ ॥
passages.en:
As the sense of one's own (corporeal) identity is present in the
intellect right up to the end of the body's existence, but not so also when the
body has come to an end,523 (an initiate's) liberation (takes place then)
because (only his) spiritual ignorance has been destroyed (by initiation). (49)

passages.section: Definitions of the Forms of Knowledge and Ignorance
passages.mula:
बौद्धाज्ञाननिवृत्तौ तु विकल्पोन्मूलनाद् ध्रुवम् ।
तदैव मोक्ष इत्युक्तं धात्रा श्रीमन्निशाटने । ५० ।।
विकल्पयुक्तचित्तस्तु पिंडपाताच्छिवं व्रजेत् ।
इतरस्तु तदैवेति शास्त्रस्यात्र प्रधानतः ।। ५१ ।।
passages.en:
(However,) liberation is most certainly (achieved) just then, when intellectual ignorance ceases, because (binding) thought has been uprooted. Thus the Benefactor has said in the venerable Nisāțanatantra: "He whose
mind is yoked (yukta) to thought attains Śiva (only) after the body dies,
whereas the other (aspirant who is free of thought attains Him) that very moment.5525* This is because here (intuitive insight into the meaning of the) 526 scriptures is primary.20 (50-51)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
ज्ञेयस्य हि परं तत्त्वं यः प्रकाशात्मकः शिवः ।
नह्यप्रकाशरूपस्य प्राकाश्यं वस्तुतापि वा ।। ५२॥
passages.en: (vastutā).536 (52)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
अवस्तुतापि भावानां चमत्कारैकगोचरा ।
यत्कुड्यसदृशी नेयं धीरवस्त्वेतदित्यपि ॥ ५३।।
passages.en:
The non-existence (avastutā) of entities is also in one (and the same)
field of the wonder (of consciousness as is their existence).540 The notion
(dhī) "this is non-existent (avastu)" is not similar to (an inert object such as)
a wall.541 (53)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
प्रकाशो नाम यश्चायं सर्वदैव प्रकाशते ।
अनपह्नवनीयत्वात् किं तस्मिन्मानकल्पनैः ।। ५४॥
passages.en:
Indeed, this Light (of consciousness) shines at all times; so, as it
cannot be denied, 54 what is the use (of applying) contrived means of knowledge to it? (All that needs be done is to recognise that the One Light
exists and that it illumines the manifestation of all things.) (54)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
प्रमाणान्यपि वस्तूनां जीवितं यानि तन्वते ।
तेषामपि परो जीवः स एव परमेश्वरः ।। ५५ ॥
passages.en:
The (many) means of knowledge give life to all things (vastu)
(because it is by means of them that they appear to the sentient subject),
while the supreme living essence (jiva) of those (means) also is that same
Supreme Lord (Himself Who is the true identity of the perceiver).550 (55)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
सर्वापह्नवहेवाकधर्माप्येवं हि वर्तते ।
ज्ञानमात्मार्थमित्येतन्नेति मां प्रति भासते ।। ५६ ।।
passages.en:
It happens in this way even to one whose capricious nature is to
deny everything, namely that (he experiences that): "this negation of
knowledge, oneself and the object manifests to me." (56)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
अप तौ साधने वा वस्तूनामाद्यमीदृशम् ।
यत्तत्र के प्रमाणानामुपत्त्युपयोगिते ।। ५७।।
passages.en:
(Insofar as) the negation or affirmation of (the existence of) things
is preceded (a priori) by such a one (who does it), how can the reasons
(based on any of the) means of knowledge be applicable there (to him)2557
(57)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
कामिके तत एवोक्तं हेतुवादविवर्जितम् ।
तस्य देवातिदेवस्य परापेक्षा न विद्यते ॥ ५८॥
परस्य तदपेक्षत्वात्स्वतन्त्रोऽयमतः स्थितः ।
अनपेक्षस्य वशिनो देशकालाकृतिक्रमाः ।। ५९ ।।
नियता नेति स विभुर्नित्यो विश्वाकृतिः शिवः
विभुत्वात्सर्वगो नित्यभावादाद्यन्तवर्जितः ।। ६० ।।
विश्वाकृतित्वाच्चिदचित्तद्वैचित्र्यावभासकः ।
ततोऽस्य बहुरूपत्वमुक्तं दीक्षोत्तरादिके ।। ६१ ।।
भुवनं विग्रहो ज्योतिः खं शब्दो मन्त्र एव च ।
बिन्दुनादादिसंभिन्नः षड्विधः शिव उच्यते ।। ६२।।
passages.en:
It is the means (sādhana) to accomplishing all Mantras. One should recollect it
always in order to attain (Siva's) world. By contemplating (Śiva's) Light constantly, the yogi attains the accomplishments of yoga. (These include) the powers to make oneself
small at will and the other (forms of) mastery that characterize the yogi's sport etc. The
form of a tiger (vyāla) and no form (at all), (such is) Supreme Śiva who pervades Space (vyomavyãpin). (16-17)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.en:
Śiva as Pervasive Space
By reflecting on the Lord (īśāna) who is all-pervasive, one attains Śiva. One
should think of the supreme Space as devoid of (phenomenal) qualities, beyond stain,
free of planets and constellations and (transparent) like pure crystal. (18-19ab)
Sound
He whose mind is merged in Space and is properly established in Space, attains
liberation where he dissolves away into Sound. By contemplating Sound, without a
doubt (one attains) liberation and accomplishments. Therefore, one should engage with all effort in the contemplation of Sound. (19cd-21ab)
(The channel of the breath called) Idã is on its left side. Its most excellent
sound is 'Ciñciņī'. This is (sound) pertaining to Nature (prākrta), which is said to be
gross. By (the influence of) the right (channel), suşumnā is said to make the sound of a
cricket (ciravāk). That is said to pertain to the individual soul (puruşa) and is said to be (the sound) of the subtle. (21cd-23ab)
The supreme (form of Sound) is in the centre, at the extremity at the end of the
cessation of the Sound of a bell. Devoid of support and without foundation, that itself is
the supreme plane. (The Sound) devoid of support and without location is at the end of (the Sound) Ciñciņī and the cricket, at the end of the cessation of the Sound of the Bell
is the (insight that) "I am Siva", which is without location. (23cd-25ab)
citrastha īśvaro nādah sa tu sākșāc chivah (chiva) smrtah
A 'world-order' is the particular world-order (in which a fettered soul)
must reside (due to his past Karma), and is the basis (of his experiences of its)
consequences (bhogādhāra). 568 The word 'form' denotes by figurative application, (divine beings) that possess a (particular) form (vigrahin).569
Once the wise man has placed the aggregate of Mantras in the Heart, he should
deposit the icon (mūrti). (Attended) by the energies and principles consisting of Brahmă
and the rest, it is considered to generate all the accomplishments. He should constantly
reflect on the Point, which is Iśvara, located there. Iśvara is Sound located in the
variegated, and that indeed is considered to be Śiva, directly apparent. (25cd-27ab)
(+ etat tat paramam guhyam etat tat paramam padam \)
The one called Harnsa, the Point, Sound and the End of Sound - having known
(this) in this way, the one who recites Mantra is stainless Śiva, directly apparent. That is
the supreme secret, that is supreme SŚiva, that is supreme knowledge, and that is the
supreme imperishable (reality). (27cd-29)
There is no higher object of meditation than this. There is no higher Śiva than
this. Once He has been known in this way, (the aspirant) is liberated - there is no doubt
here (about it). This procedure bestows upon the adept the accomplishment of all the
things (he) desires. Beyond them is the God I have taught before, who is devoid of form
and sound and pervades all the reality levels (tattva). Once having known Him, (fettered
souls) are freed, and without a doubt, are successful.' (30-32)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
यो यदात्मकतानिष्ठस्तद्भावं स प्रपद्यते ।
व्योमादिशब्दविज्ञानात् परो मोक्षो न संशयः ।। ६३।।
passages.en:
(The adept) attains the state of being which is the essential nature of
that (one out of these six aspects of Śiva) in which he is resolutely
established (niștha),583 (whereas) supreme liberation is (attained) without a
doubt by a complete knowledge (vijňāna) of the (pervasive) resonance
(śabda) of (all these aspects) starting with Space,584 (63) (64)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
विश्वाकृतित्वे देवस्य तदेतच्चोपलक्षणम् ।
अनवच्छिन्नतारूढाववच्छेदलयेऽस्य च ।। ६४ ॥
passages.en:
Moreover, as God is omniform, that (series is only) a secondary
(metaphorical) designation (of His nature in the context of) His
(progressive) ascent into (His) unconditioned state and of the dissolving
away of His limitations (into His transcendental state),593 (64) (65)

passages.section: The a priori Nature of Śiva Consciousness
passages.mula:
उक्त च कामिके देवः सवीकृतिर्निराकृतिः ।
जलदर्पणवत्तेन सर्व व्याप्तं चराचरम् ।। ६५।।
passages.en: He pervades all things, both (animate and) moving, and (as well as inanimate and) immobile, (and assumes their form)'. (65) (66)

passages.section: The Powers of Śiva's Freedom
passages.mula:
न चास्य विभुताद्योऽयं धर्मोऽन्योन्यं विभिद्यते
एक एवास्य धर्मोऽसौ सर्वाक्षेपेण वर्तते ।। ६६ ॥
तेन स्वातन्त्र्यशक्त्यैव युक्त इत्याञ्जसो विधिः ।
बहुशक्तित्वमप्यस्य तच्छक्त्यैवावियुक्तता ।। ६७।।
शक्तिश्च नाम भावस्य स्वं रूपं मातृकल्पितम् । तेनाद्वयः स एवापि शक्तिमत्परिकल्पने ।। ६८ ।।
passages.en:
The power (śakti) (which is the functional efficacy) of an entity is its
own (specific) nature, as conceived by the subjects (who perceive it) (mātrkalpita) (on the basis of its various effects). Thus (it follows) that (Śiva)
also is (one reality) without a second, (even) when He is conceived to be (power and) the possessor of power. (68) (69)

passages.section: The Powers of Śiva's Freedom
passages.mula:
मातृक्लृप्ते हि देवस्य तत्र तत्र वपुष्यलम् ।
को भेदो वस्तुतो वह्नेर्दग्धृपक्तृत्वयोरिव ।। ६९ ।।
passages.en:
Just as there is (no difference between) the fire's (capacity) to burn
and cook (and the fire itself always remains one and the same), similarly,
what difference is there in actual fact between the forms (vapuş) of God
conceived in various circumstances (tatra tatra) by the (many) perceivers?613
(69) (70)

passages.section: The Powers of Śiva's Freedom
passages.mula:
न चासौ परमार्थेन न किञ्चिद्धासनादृते ।
नह्यस्ति किञ्चित्तच्छक्तितद्वद्भेदोऽपि वास्तवः ।। ७० ।।
passages.en:
However, this (difference between powers and their possessor) is
not absolutely non-existent (rather it does exist). Nothing exists apart from
(its) manifestation; thus, the difference between power and its possessor is
also real (vāstava) (in this sense),614 (70) (71)

passages.section: The Powers of Śiva's Freedom
passages.mula:
स्वशक्त्युद्रेकजनकं तादात्म्याद्वस्तुनो हि यत् ।
शक्तिस्तदपि देव्येवं भान्त्यप्यन्यस्वरूपिणी ।। ७१ ।।
passages.en:
What an entity possesses that, by virtue of its oneness with it,
generates an abundance of its own powers, is also a power. (Similarly, the
Lord has only one power, namely) the Goddess, Who even though She
manifests in this way, transcends (Her manifestations).615 (71) (72)

passages.section: The Powers of Śiva's Freedom
passages.mula:
शिवश्चालुप्तविभवस्तथा सृष्टोऽवभासते ।
स्वसंविन्मातृमकुरे स्वातन्त्र्याद्भावनादिषु ।। ७२।।
passages.en:
It is by virtue of (His) freedom that Śiva (also), without being
deprived of His glorious power (vibhava), manifests in this way in the
course of creative meditation (bhāvanā) and the like, created (srşta) within
the mirror of (the consciousness of the individual) perceiver, whose
consciousness is (in fact) His own.17 (72) (73)

passages.section: The Powers of Śiva's Freedom
passages.mula:
तस्माद्येन मुखेनैष भात्यनंशोऽपि तत्तथा ।
शक्तिरित्येष वस्त्वेव शक्तितद्वत्क्रमः स्फुटः ।। ७३ ।।
passages.en: succession from power to its possessor is an evident (sphuța) reality (vastu). (73) (74)

passages.section: The Powers of Śiva's Freedom
passages.mula:
श्रीमत्किरणशास्त्रे च तत्प्रश्नोत्तरपूर्वकम् ।
अनुभावो विकल्पोऽपि मानसो न मनः शिवे ।। ७४ ॥
अविज्ञाय शिवं दीक्षा कथमित्यत्र चोत्तरम् ।
क्षुधाद्यनुभवो नैव विकल्पो नहि मानसः ।। ७५ ।।
रसाद्यनध्यक्षत्वेऽपि रूपादेव यथा तरुम् ।
विकल्पो वेत्ति तद्वत्तु नादबिन्द्वादिना शिवम् ।। ७६ ॥
passages.en:
(Anyway Śiva can also be realized by thought). Just as a notion
knows a tree by its form alone even when its taste etc. is not perceived,
similarly, Śiva (is known) by means (of His powers that are aspects of His
nature, such as Divine) Sound (nāda), Light (bindu) and the like.648 (76) (77)

passages.section: The Powers of Śiva's Freedom
passages.mula:
बहुशक्तित्वमस्योक्तं शिवस्य यदतो महान् ।
कलातत्त्वपुराणीणुपदादिभेदविस्तरः ।। ७७।।
सृष्टिस्थितितिरोधानसंहारानुग्रहादि च ।
तुर्यमित्यपि देवस्य बहुशक्तित्वजृम्भितम् ।। ७८ ।।
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तान्यतदतीतानि यान्यपि ।
तान्यप्यमुष्य नाथस्य स्वातन्त्र्यलहरीभरः ।। ७९ ।।
महामन्त्रेशमन्त्रेशमन्त्राः शिवपुरोगमाः ।
अकलौ सकलश्चेति शिवस्यैव विभूतयः ।। ८० ।
passages.en:
bahuśaktitvam asyoktam śivasya yad ato mahān
655The many powers Śiva is said to possess are the great extension of
differentiation (bheda) (of the Paths of manifestation consisting of) the
cosmic forces (kalā), metaphysical principles (tattva), and world-orders
(pura),556 (along with their respective denotators, namely the Paths of the)
letters, Mantras, parts of Mantras (pada) and the rest. The unfolding of the
Lord's manifold power (also consists of the processes of) creation,
persistence, obscuration, withdrawal and grace etc. as well as the Fourth
(state).
Moreover, (the states of) waking, dreaming and deep sleep and
others beyond them57 are all the multitude of the waves of the Lord's
(creative) freedom (svātantrya). So too (the perceivers) headed by Śiva
(called) the Great Lords of Mantra, the Lords of Mantra and Mantras,
(along with) the two that are Deconditioned (ākala) and the Conditioned
(sakala), are (all) the glorious powers (vibhūti) of Śiva Himself.658 (77-80)

The Powers of Śiva's Freedom

passages.section: The Innate Nature of the Group (grāmadharma)
passages.mula:
तत्त्वग्रामस्य सर्वस्य धर्मः स्यादनपायवान् ।
आत्मैव हि स्वभावात्मेत्युक्तं श्रीत्रिशिरोमते ।। ८१ ।।
passages.en:
It is said in the venerable Triśiromata that the (essential) nature
(dharma) of the (entire) group (grāma) of metaphysical principles (tattva) is
imperishable. Indeed, it is the Self alone who is the identity of their own
nature (svabhāvātman). (81) (82)

passages.section: The Innate Nature of the Group (grāmadharma)
passages.mula:
हृदिस्थं सर्वदेहस्थं स्वभावस्थं सुसूक्ष्मकम् ।
सामूह्यं चैव तत्त्वानां ग्रामशब्देन कीर्तितम् ।। ८२॥
passages.en:
The extremely subtle totality (sāmūhya) of the principles located in
the Heart, in all the body, and in the specific nature (svabhāva) (of all things), is termed the 'group' (grāma).661 (82) (83)

passages.section: Established in Rāma (rāmastha)
passages.mula:
आत्मैव धर्म इत्युक्तः शिवामृतपरिप्लुतः ।
प्रकाशावस्थितं ज्ञानं भावाभावादिमध्यतः ।। ८३।।
स्वस्थाने वर्तनं ज्ञेयं द्रष्टृत्वं विगतावृति ।
विविक्तवस्तुकथितशुद्धविज्ञाननिर्मलः ॥ ८४॥
ग्रामधर्मवृत्तिरुक्तस्तस्य सर्व प्रसिद्धयति ।
ऊवं त्यक्त्वाधो विशेत्स रामस्थो मध्यदेशगः ॥ ८५॥
गतिः स्थानं स्वप्नजाग्रदुन्मेषणनिमेषणे ।
धावनं प्लवनं चैव आयासः शक्तिवेदनम् ।। ८६ ।।
बुद्धिभेदास्तथा भावाः संज्ञाः कर्माण्यनेकशः ।
एष रामो व्यापकोऽत्र शिवः परमकारणम् ।। ८७।।
passages.en:
695This delight (rāma) is movement, standing (still), dreaming (the
dream of thought constructs) and waking (to the insight of knowledge). (It
is) the opening and closing of the eyes, running, jumping, exerting an effort
(in knowledge and ignorance) (āyāsa), the experience of the energies (of the
senses), the (various) forms of the intellect (buddhi), entities, names and
countless actions. 696It is Śiva, the supreme (omnipresent) cause, who
pervades (everything) here. (86-87) (87-88)

passages.section: Degrees of Freedom and Obscuration
passages.mula:
कल्मषक्षीणमनसा स्मृतिमात्रनिरोधनात् ।
ध्यायते परमं ध्येयं गमागमपदे स्थितम् ।। ८८ ॥
परं शिवं तु व्रजति भैरवाख्यं जपादपि ।
तत्स्वरूपं जपः प्रोक्तो भावाभावपदच्युतः ।। ८९ ।।
तदत्रापि तदीयेन स्वातन्त्र्येणोपकल्पितः ।
दूरासन्नादिको भेदश्चित्स्वातन्त्र्यव्यपेक्षया ।। ९० ।।
passages.en:
Here (in this case) also, (it is clear that) the difference (between the
means to realisation) conceived by (the Lord's) freedom as being, for
example, (more or less) close or distant (from their goal)717 is with regards
to (the degrees of) freedom of consciousness (citsvātantrya). (90) (91)

passages.section: Degrees of Freedom and Obscuration
passages.mula:
एवं स्वातन्त्र्यपूर्णत्वादतिदुर्घटकार्ययम् ।
केन नाम न रूपेण भासते परमेश्वरः ।। ९१ ।।
passages.en:
In what form does the Supreme Lord not appear by virtue of the
fullness (of His) freedom in this way? (Verily,) He accomplishes miracles!720 (91) (92)

passages.section: Degrees of Freedom and Obscuration
passages.mula:
निरावरणमाभाति भात्यावृतनिजात्मकः ।
आवृतानावृतो भाति बहुधा भेदसङ्गमात् ।। ९२॥
इति शक्तित्रयं नाथे स्वातन्त्र्यापरनामकम् ।
इच्छादिभिरभिख्याभिर्गुरुभिः प्रकटीकृतम् ।। ९३॥

passages.section: The Etymology of the Names of Bhairava, Deva and Pati
passages.mula:
देवो ह्यन्वर्थशास्त्रोक्तैः शब्दैः समुपदिश्यते ।
महाभैरवदेवोऽयं पतिर्यः परमः शिवः ।। ९४॥
passages.en:
(The nature of) God (deva) is taught by means of words stated in the scriptures (that serve as etymologies), the meanings of which are in
accord with His nature. He is this great Bhairava, the Lord (Pati) and Supreme Śiva.727 (94) (95)

passages.section: The Etymology of the Names of Bhairava, Deva and Pati
passages.mula:
विश्वं बिभर्ति पोषणधारणयोगेन तेन च भ्रियते ।
स्वविमर्शतया रव

द्योतनमस्य स्तुतिर्यतः सकलम् ।। १०१ ।।
तत्प्रवणमात्मलाभात्
प्रभृति समस्तेऽपि कर्तव्ये
बोधात्मकः समस्तक्रियामयो दृक्क्रियागुणश्च गतिः ।। १०२॥

passages.section: The Etymology of the Names of Bhairava, Deva and Pati
passages.mula:
इति निर्वचनैः शिवतनु-
शास्त्रे गुरुभिः स्मृतो देवः ।
शासनरोधनपालनपाचनयोगात्स सर्वमुपकुरुते ।। १०३ ।।
तेन पतिः श्रेयोमय
एव शिवो नाशिवं किमपि तत्र
passages.en:
tena patih śreyomaya
He is (called) the 'Lord' (pati) because by teaching (śāsana),
obstructing (rodhana), protecting (pālana) and maturing (pācana) (Karma),761 He helps all beings. He is Siva (the Auspicious One) (because)
He is the supreme good (śreyomaya)762 and there is nothing inauspicious
(aśiva) there (within Him). (103cd-104ab) (104)

passages.section: The Etymology of the Names of Bhairava, Deva and Pati
passages.mula:
ईदृग्रूपं कियदपि
रुद्रोपेन्द्रादिषु स्फुरेद्येन ।। १०४ ।।
तेनावच्छेदनुदे
परममहत्पदविशेषणमुपात्तम्
passages.en:
tenāvacchedanude
This same kind of nature is also manifest to a certain degree (in the
minor gods) such as Rudra and Upendra. Thus, the adjectives 'supreme'
and 'great' are added (to His name) to preclude (the mistaken idea that) Hе
is limited.768 (104cd-105ab) (105)

passages.section: The Exposition of the Tantrāloka
passages.mula:
इति यज्ज्ञेयसतत्त्वं दर्शयते तच्छिवाज्ञया ।। १०५ ।।
मया स्वसंवित्सत्तर्कपतिशास्त्रत्रिकक्रमात् ।
passages.en:
Thus, I will expound, at Siva's command, according to my own
consciousness, sound discriminative reasoning (sattarka), Śaiva doctrine
(patiśāstra),769 Trika and Krama,770 the true nature of what needs be known.
(105cd-106ab) (106)

passages.section: The Deployment of Bhairava's Energies and the Supremacy
passages.mula:
तस्य शक्तय एवैतास्तिस्रो भान्ति परादिकाः ।। १०६ ॥
सृष्टौ स्थितौ लये तुर्ये तेनैता द्वादशोदिताः ।
passages.en:
(Śiva) has just these three powers, namely, (the Goddess) Parā
(Supreme) and the rest (that is, Parāparā (Middling) and Aparā (Lower)).
They manifest in (the phases of) creation, persistence, withdrawal and the
Fourth (that both includes and transcends them),778 Thus (they) have arisen twelve-fold.779 (106cd-107ab) (107)

passages.section: The Deployment of Bhairava's Energies and the Supremacy
passages.mula:
तावान्पूर्णस्वभावोऽसौ परमः शिव उच्यते ।। १०७ ।।
तेनात्रोपासकाः साक्षात्तत्रैव परिनिष्ठिताः ।
passages.en:
He who is this much (tāvān) is full (and complete), and (so) is said to
be Supreme Śiva. Thus, those who worship (these twelve aspects) here are
evidently well-established there (in Śiva's nature). (107cd-108ab) (108)

passages.section: The Deployment of Bhairava's Energies and the Supremacy
passages.mula:
तासामपि च भेदांशन्यूनाधिक्यादियोजनम् ।। १०८ ।।
तत्स्वातन्त्र्यबलादेव शास्त्रेषु परिभाषितम् ।
passages.en:
The scriptures explain that the conjunction of these (powers) with a
greater or lesser (number of) differentiated aspects (bhedāmśa) etc. takes
place by the power of His (creative) freedom. (108cd-109ab) (109)

passages.section: The Deployment of Bhairava's Energies and the Supremacy
passages.mula:
एकवीरो यामलोऽथ त्रिशक्तिश्चतुरात्मकः ।। १०९ ।। पञ्चमूर्तिः षडात्मायं सप्तकोऽष्टकभूषितः ।
नवात्मा दशदिक्छक्तिरेकादशकलात्मकः ।। ११० ।।
द्वादशारमहाचक्रनायको भैरवः स्थितः ।
passages.en:
three powers, as four-fold,71 with five iconic forms, as six-fold, as this
group of seven and adorned with the group of eight,792 as the Nine-fold One
(navātman), as possessing the powers of the ten directions, and as the eleven
energies.7"3 (109cd-111ab) (110-111)

passages.section: The Deployment of Bhairava's Energies and the Supremacy
passages.mula:
एवं यावत्सहस्रारे निःसंख्यारेऽपि वा प्रभुः ।। १११ ।।
विश्वचक्रे महेशानो विश्वशक्तिर्विजृम्भते ।
passages.en:
In this way, the Great Lord, (all) powerful,506 who is (Himself) all
the powers, unfolds within (the one Wheel which is) all the Wheels
(viśvacakra), until (He expands) into the Wheel of a Thousand Spokes,807 or
even within that of countless spokes, 508 (111cd-112ab) (112)

passages.section: The Deployment of Bhairava's Energies and the Supremacy
passages.mula:
तेषामपि च चक्राणां स्ववर्गानुगमात्मना ।। ११२ ।।
ऐक्येन चक्रगो भेदस्तत्र तत्र निरूपितः ।
passages.en:
The difference between those configurations (cakra) also is
described in various places (in the scriptures), (each) as an (encompassing)
unity, the nature of which accords with the category to which it belongs
(according to its function). (112cd-113ab) (113)

passages.section: The Deployment of Bhairava's Energies and the Supremacy
passages.mula:
चतुष्षडर्द्विर्द्विगणनायोगात्रैशिरसे मते ।। ११३ ।।
षट्चक्रेश्वरता नाथस्योक्ता चित्रा निजातिः ।
passages.en:
The mastery of the six wheels of the Lord's own form is said in the
Traiśirasamata to be wonderfully various813 by virtue of His union with
four, six and twice times twice those (powers).814 (113cd-114ab) (114)

passages.section: The Deployment of Bhairava's Energies and the Supremacy
passages.mula:
नामानि चक्रदेवीनां तत्र कृत्यविभेदतः ।। ११४ ।
सौम्यरौद्राकृतिध्यानयोगीन्यन्वर्थकल्पनात्
passages.en:
817The names of the goddesses of the Wheels there (vary) according
to their various functions. (They do so also) because they are conceived in
accord with their purpose, (nature and the meaning of their name)
(anvarthakalpana), in association with the visualization (dhyāna) of (this or
that) peaceful (saumya) or fierce (raudra) form.818 (114cd-115ab) (115)

passages.section: The Nourishing Power of the Creative Imagination (pratibhā)
passages.mula:
एकस्य संविन्नाथस्य ह्यान्तरी प्रतिभा तनुः ।। ११५ ।।
सौम्यं वान्यन्मितं संविदूर्मिचक्रमुपास्यते ।
passages.en: manifest thereby), whether peaceful or otherwise. (115cd-116ab) (116)

passages.section: The Nourishing Power of the Creative Imagination (pratibhā)
passages.mula:
अस्य स्यात्पुष्टिरित्येषा संविद्देवी तथोदितात् ।। ११६ ।।
ध्यानात्सञ्जल्पसंमिश्राद् व्यापाराच्चापि बाह्यतः
स्फुटीभूता सती भाति तस्य तादृक्फलप्रदा ।। ११७।।
पुष्टिः शुष्कस्य सरसीभावो जलमतः सितम् ।
अनुगम्य ततो ध्यानं तत्प्रधानं प्रतन्यते ।। ११८ ।।
ये च स्वभावतो वर्णा रसनिःष्यन्दिनो यथा ।
दन्त्यौष्ठ्यदन्त्यप्रायास्ते कैश्चिद्वर्णैः कृताः सह ।। ११९ ।।
तं बीजभावमागत्य संविदं स्फुटयन्ति ताम् ।
पुष्टिं कुरु रसेनैनमाप्याययतरामिति ।। १२० ।।
सञ्जल्पोऽपि विकल्पात्मा किं तामेव न पूरयेत् ।
अमृतेयमिदं क्षीरमिदं सर्पिर्बलावहम् ।। १२१ ।।
तेनास्य बीजं पुष्णीयामित्येनां पूरयेत्क्रियाम् ।

passages.section: Limited and Unlimited Deities are Forms of the Lord of Consciousness
passages.mula:
तस्माद्विश्वेश्वरो बोधभैरवः समुपास्यते ।। १२२ ।।
अवच्छेदानवच्छिद्भ्यां भोगमोक्षार्थिभिर्जनैः ।
passages.en:
Therefore, the Lord of the universe (viśveśvara), the Bhairava Who
is Consciousness (bodhabhairava), is worshipped by those who desire
worldly benefits (bhoga) or liberation, with a (specific) limited (form) or
without limitation, (respectively). (122cd-123ab) (123)

passages.section: Injunctions do not Apply to the Supreme Deity Who is the Ultimate Goal
passages.mula:
येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता इत्यतो गुरुरादिशत् ।। १२३ ।।
ये बोधाव्यतिरिक्तं हि किञ्चिद्याज्यतया विदुः ।
तेऽपि वेद्यं विविञ्चाना बोधाभेदेन मन्वते ।। १२४ ।।
तेनाविच्छिन्नतामर्शरूपाहन्ताप्रथात्मनः ।
स्वयंप्रथस्य न विधिः सृष्ट्यात्मास्य च पूर्वगः ।। १२५ ॥
वेद्या हि देवतासृष्टिः शक्तेर्हेतोः समुत्थिता
अहंरूपा तु संवित्तिर्नित्या स्वप्रथनात्मिका ।। १२६ ।।
विधिर्नियोगस्त्र्यंशा च भावना चोदनात्मिका
तदेकसिद्धा इन्द्राद्या विधिपूर्वी हि देवताः ।। १२७ ।।
अहंबोधस्तु न तथा ते तु संवेद्यरूपताम् ।
उन्मग्नामेव पश्यन्तस्तं विदन्तोऽपि नो विदुः ॥ १२८ ।।
तदुक्तं न विदुम तु तत्त्वेनातश्चलन्ति ते ।
passages.en:
(However), only (minor) deities such as Indra, (whose worship) is indeed ordained by injunctions (vidhipūrva), are attained that way. This is not the case with 'I' consciousness. Those (who sacrifice to consciousness
but) witness only (its) emergent (unmagna) objective aspect, although they
know that (consciousness in this aspect as deity, in truth) know it not. That is said (in the Bhagavadgītā, where we read that): 'they do not know Me in reality and so they fall (calanti).9867 (127cd-129ab) (128-129)

passages.section: Injunctions do not Apply to the Supreme Deity Who is the Ultimate Goal
passages.mula:
चलनं तु व्यवच्छिन्नरूपतापत्तिरेव या ।। १२९॥
देवान्देवयजो यान्तीत्यादि तेन न्यरूप्यत ।
passages.en:
This is why (Krşna) has said: “they go to the gods who worship the
gods.,874 (130ab) (130)

passages.section: Injunctions do not Apply to the Supreme Deity Who is the Ultimate Goal
passages.mula:
निमज्ज्य वेद्यतां ये तु तत्र संविन्मयीं स्थितिम् ।। १३० ।।
विदुस्ते ह्यनवच्छिन्नं तद्भक्ता अपि यान्ति माम् ।
passages.en:
However, those who, having submerged (these gods') objectively
perceivable nature (into consciousness), know there the abiding state (sthiti)
(of reality) which is (pure) consciousness.$76 (Thus says Krşņa,) "even
though they are devoted to that (particular divine form), they go to Me who
am unconditioned." (130cd-131ab) (131)

passages.section: Injunctions do not Apply to the Supreme Deity Who is the Ultimate Goal
passages.mula:
सर्वत्रात्र ह्यहंशब्दो बोधमात्रैकवाचकः ।। १३१ ।
स भोक्तृप्रभुशब्दाभ्यां याज्ययष्टृतयोदितः

passages.section: Injunctions do not Apply to the Supreme Deity Who is the Ultimate Goal
passages.mula:
याजमानी संविदेव याज्या नान्येति चोदितम् ।। १३२ ।।
नाकृतिः कुतोऽप्यन्या देवता न हि सोचिता ।
passages.en:
It is said that consciousness itself is the sacrificer and that the
object to which sacrifice is offered is none other than that. (Deity has) no
other form (than this) at all (kuto 'pi).883 (For) another deity (than this) is
not appropriate (as an object of worship).884 (132cd-133ab) (133)

passages.section: Obscured and Unobscured Consciousness
passages.mula:
विधिश्च नोक्तः कोऽप्यत्र मन्त्रादि वृत्तिधाम वा ।। १३३।।
सोऽयमात्मानमावृत्य स्थितो जडपदं गतः ।
आवृतानावृतात्मा तु देवादिस्थावरान्तगः ।। १३४।।
जडाजडस्याप्येतस्य द्वैरूप्यस्यास्ति चित्रता ।
तस्य स्वतन्त्रभावो हि किं किं यन्न विचिन्तयेत् ।। १३५ ।।
तदुक्तं त्रिशिरःशास्त्रे संबुद्ध इति वेत्ति यः ।
passages.en:
He (the Lord of Consciousness) is free. What may He not
conceive?899 That is said in the Triśiraḥśāstra, (which declares that) one who
knows (this wonderful diversity) is well awake (sambuddha). (135cd-136ab)
(136)

passages.section: Obscured and Unobscured Consciousness
passages.mula:
ज्ञेयभावो हि चिद्धर्मस्तच्छायाच्छादयेन्न ताम् ।। १३६॥
तेनाजडस्य भागस्य पुद्गलाण्वादिसंज्ञिनः ।
अनावरणभागांशे वैचित्र्यं बहुधा स्थितम् ।। १३७ ।।
passages.en:
Thus, the wonderful variety of that sentient aspect (variously) called, for example, the individual soul (pudgala) or atom (of consciousness)
(anu), rests in many ways in the aspect (of consciousness) that is unobscured. (137)

passages.section: Obscured and Unobscured Consciousness
passages.mula:
संविद्रूपे न भेदोऽस्ति वास्तवो यद्यपि ध्रुवे ।
तथाप्यावृतिनिह्रसतारतम्यात्स लक्ष्यते ।। १३८ ।।
passages.en:
Although there is no real division (bheda) (of levels) within
consciousness, which is always stable (dhruva) (and invariable), even so it is perceived (to exist) due to the gradation (of the progressive) decrease of the veil (that covers it). (138)

passages.section: Obscured and Unobscured Consciousness
passages.mula:
तद्विस्तरेण वक्ष्यामः शक्तिपातविनिर्णये ।
समाप्य परतां स्थौल्यप्रसङ्गे चर्चयिष्यते ।। १३९ ॥
passages.en:
We will talk about that extensively in the course of explaining (the
nature of) the descent of the power (of grace) (śaktipāta),905 and having
concluded (the matter) present in the first (part), it will be discussed in the
context of matters pertaining to ritual (sthaulyaprasanga) (in the second part).506 906 (139)

passages.section: Preliminary Analysis of the Means based on Will, Knowledge and Action
passages.mula: पूर्णमेव निजं रूपं कंचिदंशांशिकाक्रमात् ।। १४० ।।
passages.en:
Thus, while the Pervasive Lord (vibhu) reveals His own complete
form (in all His fullness) to a certain perceiver (pramātr), (He does so) to
some (other) part by part, successively. (140)

passages.section: Preliminary Analysis of the Means based on Will, Knowledge and Action
passages.mula:
विश्वभावैकभावात्मस्वरूपप्रथनं हि यत् ।
अणूनां तत्परं ज्ञानं तदन्यदपरं बहु ।। १४१ ।।
passages.en:
The (full and complete) experience (prathana)914 of one's own
nature as the one Being (bhāva) of all beings is the supreme (para)
knowledge (of Deity) individual souls possess. Inferior (apara) and multiple
is that (knowledge) which is other than that. (141)

passages.section: Preliminary Analysis of the Means based on Will, Knowledge and Action
passages.mula:
तच्च साक्षादुपायेन तदुपायादिनापि च ।
प्रथमानं विचित्राभिर्संगीभिरिह भिद्यते ।। १४२ ।।
passages.en:
And that (knowledge), revealed (prathamāna)916 through the means
that is direct as well as (those that are) means to that (direct means) etc., is
divided here into (wonderfully) diverse (vicitra) modalities.917 (142)

passages.section: Preliminary Analysis of the Means based on Will, Knowledge and Action
passages.mula:
तत्रापि स्वपरद्वारद्वारित्वात्सर्वशोंशशः ।
व्यवधानाव्यवधिना भूयान्भेदः प्रवर्तते ।। १४३ ।।
passages.en:
tatrāpi svaparadvāradvāritvāt sarvaśo 'mśaśah
There (in that case) also, these (means are of) many kinds, according to whether they are (direct or) mediated with regard to
themselves or another, in all respects or part by part, with or without
interposed (obstacles). (143)

passages.section: Preliminary Analysis of the Means based on Will, Knowledge and Action
passages.mula:
ज्ञानस्य चाभ्युपायो यो न तदज्ञानमुच्यते ।
ज्ञानमेव तु तत्सूक्ष्मं परं त्विच्छात्मकं मतम् ।। १४४ ॥
passages.en:
is more subtle than that is considered to be the supreme (means). It is (the
power of) the will (icchā) (to realisation that achieves its goal
instantaneously).927 (144)

passages.section: Preliminary Analysis of the Means based on Will, Knowledge and Action
passages.mula:
उपायोपेयभावस्तु ज्ञानस्य स्थौल्यविभ्रमः ।
एषैव च क्रियाशक्तिर्बन्धमोक्षैककारणम् ।। १४५ ।।
passages.en:
(The sense that there is) a condition which is the means and one
that is a goal is (essentially) an error (inherent in) the gross state of
knowledge, and that is itself the power of action, which is the sole cause
of (both) bondage and liberation.930 (145)

passages.section: Preliminary Analysis of the Means based on Will, Knowledge and Action
passages.mula:
तत्राद्ये स्वपरामर्शे निर्विकल्पैकधामनि ।
यत्स्फुरेत्प्रकटं साक्षात्तदिच्छाख्यं प्रकीर्त्तितम् ।। १४६ ।।
passages.en:
9341) There (as that is so), that which manifests clearly in the first
(moment of perception) within one's own self-awareness, the sole abode (of
pure) thought-free (consciousness), is said to be the direct (sākşāt) (means
to realisation) called the will (icchã). (146)

passages.section: Preliminary Analysis of the Means based on Will, Knowledge and Action
passages.mula:
यथा विस्फारितदृशामनुसन्धिं विनाप्यलम्
भाति भावः स्फुटस्तद्वत्केषामपि शिवात्मता ।। १४७ ।।
भूयो भूयो विकल्पांशनिश्चयक्रमचर्चनात् ।
यत्परामर्शमभ्येति ज्ञानोपायं तु तद्विदुः ।। १४८ ।।
passages.en: be indeed the means based on knowledge.938 (147-148)

passages.section: Preliminary Analysis of the Means based on Will, Knowledge and Action
passages.mula:

passages.en:
3) Whereas the means based on action is taught to be (that which
utilizes as a) means (sādhana) an external entity (artha) fashioned (to serve

(between the means) is not (in their goal, which is) liberation.246 (149)

passages.section: Knowledge Extends into Action and Develops into Yoga
passages.mula:

रूढेर्योगान्ततां प्राप्तमिति श्रीगमशासने ।। १५० Π
passages.en:

passages.section: Knowledge Extends into Action and Develops into Yoga
passages.mula:
योगो नान्यः क्रिया नान्या तत्त्वारूढा हि या मतिः ।
स्वचित्तवासनाशान्तौ सा क्रियेत्यभिधीयते ।। १५१ ।।
passages.en:

own mind, is termed action. 955 (151)

passages.section: Knowledge Extends into Action and Develops into Yoga
passages.mula:
स्वचित्ते वासनाः कर्ममलमायाप्रसूतयः ।
तासां शान्तिनिमित्तं या मतिः संवित्स्वभाविका ॥ १५२ ॥
सा देहारम्भिबाह्यस्थतत्त्वव्राताधिशायिनी
क्रिया सैव च योगः स्यात्तत्त्वानां चिल्लयीकृतौ ।। १५३ ॥
passages.en:
957The latent impressions in one's own mind are the products of the
(three impurities, namely,) Ānava, Māyiya and Karma,958 958 The insight (mati)
(He is variously described in this way) here and there in the (corpus of)
scripture. Even so:
'O mistress of the gods, (ritual) action and Yoga (both) bestow (their) fruit and
are rooted in knowledge. Ritual action and Yoga are not perceived to belong to
separate category apart from knowledge.' (16/67)

passages.section: Knowledge Extends into Action and Develops into Yoga
passages.en:
